messages:
jane_cust: Hey team — our private VPC deployment started returning bursts of 429s this morning after a scheduled nightly batch. Happens for ~30s every 10m. No code change on our side. We run a customer-managed gateway (Go sidecar) in front of pods. Any tips?

elaine_support: sorry you hit this — can you share a sample request id / x-request-id header when it happened and an approximate window? also which gateway version?

jane_cust: request id x-rid=rcp-9a3f, seen 03:12:47-03:13:14 UTC. gateway v1.4.2 (custom build). We have k8s nginx-ingress in front of the sidecar, plus nodeport svc.

mike_sre: quick checklist: check envoy/sidecar local rate limiter, node-level iptables conntrack limits, and k8s ingress annotations for burst. Do you have metrics from the sidecar on token bucket state?

jane_cust: we don't expose token metrics currently. We can run a k6 rps load to reproduce.

sam_eng: for repro try this from a client inside the VPC to remove external network noise:
```
k6 run --vus 50 --duration 1m script.js
# or simple loop:
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -H "x-request-id: test-$i" https://svc.internal/api & done
```
When we hit it, check `iptables -L -v -n` and `ss -s` on the node. Also capture sidecar logs: `kubectl logs -c gateway -n app ns --since=5m`

jane_cust: ran the loop, reproduced. Sidecar logs show a lot of "rate_limited: true" and then 502s from upstream for some requests.

mike_sre: that pattern suggests the sidecar is locally refusing requests (429) and upstream failures (502) come from connection surge causing upstream queue exhaustion. Two parallel areas to tune: 1) rate limiter parameters (burst/token refill) in the customer gateway, 2) smoothing at ingress controller to avoid synchronized bursts.

elaine_support: can you paste the gateway config snippet for the limiter? typically we look for `burst`, `capacity`, and `refill_interval_ms`.

jane_cust: here is the limiter cfg in their YAML: 
```
rate_limiter:
  capacity: 100
  refill_tokens: 10
  refill_interval_ms: 1000
  max_burst: 50
```
We thought capacity=100 would be enough.

sam_eng: that config is aggressive on refill but low capacity vs concurrent connections. If many clients open at once you will exhaust tokens quickly and then all clients pause and retry — synchronized retries create the 30s spike. Two recommendations: increase capacity and add jittered backoff on client retry; or add a leaky-smoothing layer at ingress.

mike_sre: concrete quick fixes to try: increase `capacity` to 500 and `max_burst` to 200, or change `refill_interval_ms` to 200 and `refill_tokens` to 25 so tokens replenish faster proportionally. Also enable a tiny local queue (request buffer) to smooth sudden spikes instead of immediate 429.

elaine_support: on the nginx-ingress side add `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps` and `limit-burst` annotations or use the built-in rate-limiting Lua plugin to set a smoothing window. Example:
```
annotations:
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "150"
```
That prevents the entire burst from reaching the gateway at once.

jane_cust: we don't want to over-provision tokens forever. Any tips for telemetry we should add to observe this?

sam_eng: add metrics for token_count, tokens_acquired, tokens_rejected, reject_reason, and an exponential moving average for incoming rps. Also export per-route 429 counters and carve them by x-request-id while you're debugging.

mike_sre: also check node `conntrack` settings — on heavy short-lived connections you can hit conntrack table limits and start dropping/connect failures that look like 502s. Commands: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l`. If close to max, bump to accommodate bursts and tune `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`.

jane_cust: noted. We checked conntrack and it was near 80% of default. Increasing helped reduce the 502s in the repro.

elaine_support: final troubleshooting checklist we recommend you run and share results for escalations:
1) reproduce with internal k6/curl, capture request ids
2) sidecar token metrics (token_count, rejected) for the window
3) ingress burst annotations + check 429 distribution
4) node conntrack and socket stats (ss -s)
5) sidecar logs with debug for rate_limiter
6) sample tcpdump if upstream errors persist

jane_cust: thanks — we'll try config tweaks (capacity -> 500, max_burst -> 200, add ingress limit-burst) and re-run. I'll post results. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3342 for ongoing customer VPC burst 429s. Owner: elaine_support.

mike_sre: if you can, enable jittered retry on clients (randomized small backoff) so retries don't align. Happy to review the metrics after you run the tests.

jane_cust: update: after increasing capacity/burst and adding ingress smoothing the 30s spike is gone in two runs. We'll keep monitoring and add the token metrics. Thanks all! :rocket:
